editorial.thesis: A healthcare-and-banking city of about 71,000. Its retail is heavy on banks & atms and pharmacy & health retail, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and cafés, tea & coffee — and 13% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 25% of Hyderabad's. 8.45 chain outlets per lakh residents against 33.58 in Hyderabad; 5 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 2, Café Coffee Day 1, Reliance Smart / Fresh 1.

The mapped economy leans to healthcare. Shares of all mapped places: healthcare 21.1% (Hyderabad 10.3%); banks & finance 10.1% (Hyderabad 8.1%). Raw counts would mislead because Hyderabad is mapped more completely (62,819 places against 308), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 1 zones hold 13% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Gunj alone has about 7,000 residents and 0 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Hyderabad. 51% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Hyderabad 43%). The largest cores are Bhongir (145 places) and Gunj (7).

The widest brand gaps against Hyderabad. Apollo Pharmacy 2 outlets vs 348; MedPlus 1 outlets vs 150; Reliance Trends 0 outlets vs 89. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 5 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Hyderabad, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Bhongir and Gunj are the largest zones by residents (50,000 and 7,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 51% of all commercial places, and Bhongir alone lists 145.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Bhongir holds 6 of the 6 tracked chain outlets, and Gunj adds 0.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Bhongir and Gunj lead on education places (19 and 4, with 1 and 1 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Gunj. The blue cores include Bhongir.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (62,819 places in Hyderabad against 308 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Hyderabad; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Hyderabad, Bhongir's mapped places over-index on healthcare (21.1% vs 10.3%), banks & finance (10.1% vs 8.1%), education (12.3% vs 10.4%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 6 outlets of 5 tracked national brands within 5 km — 8.45 per lakh residents against Hyderabad's 33.58 (1440 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Hyderabad are Apollo Pharmacy (2 vs 348); MedPlus (1 vs 150); Reliance Trends (0 vs 89). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Hyderabad's, so low means thin by Hyderabad's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 5 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Bhongir's age mix against Hyderabad: children (0–14) 21.1% vs 24.6%, 15–24 20.0% vs 20.4%, working age 47.8% vs 48.0%, 60+ 11.1% vs 7.0%. Under-25s are 41% of residents.

zones.508116: About 50,000 residents, 145 mapped places (retail depth index 105), 6 chain outlets.
zones.508117: An under-served zone: about 7,000 residents, 7 mapped places, 0 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 35.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 2.3% of mapped places against 5.0% in Hyderabad — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Biryani By Kilo, Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 0.3% of mapped places against 2.3% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 1 (Hyderabad 78). No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.0% of mapped places against 0.8% in Hyderabad — below its share.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.6% of mapped places against 2.1% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 1 (Hyderabad 42). No mapped outlet in either city: Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.6% of mapped places against 1.3% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 2 (Hyderabad 348), MedPlus 1 (Hyderabad 150). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 3.2% of mapped places against 5.8% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 1 (Hyderabad 70).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 10.1% of mapped places against 8.1% in Hyderabad — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 1.6% of mapped places against 2.8% in Hyderabad — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 1.3% of mapped places against 3.5% in Hyderabad — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
